original_title: Elucidation of the Final Step in the Biosynthesis of Bacillithiol Reveals tRNA-Dependent Ligation of Cysteine
title: Bacillithiol's last biosynthetic step needed a tRNA
blurb: The cysteine-transfer step that closes out bacillithiol biosynthesis runs through BshC, a gene sitting outside the bacillithiol cluster, and BshC needs cysteinyl-tRNA to ligate the cysteine. A redox-cofactor pathway borrowing the translation machinery for a job that has nothing to do with making protein.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dosimetry Software Platforms Show Systematic Dose Discrepancies in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy - Bioengineer.org
title: Dosimetry software disagrees with itself on radiopharmaceutical dose
blurb: Different dosimetry platforms calculating doses for the same radiopharmaceutical therapy patient aren't converging, and the discrepancies look systematic rather than noise. Which program does your dosing shouldn't change the number this much.

original_title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
title: Recruiting more than one deubiquitinase at a time
blurb: Standard DUBTACs lean on a single deubiquitinase to stabilize a target protein; this version routes through one recruiter to engage several DUBs at once. More engagement options for a strategy that's mostly been a one-DUB trick so far.

original_title: Biodegradable Neo-Bone-Responsive Scaffold Fabricated by Organic-Inorganic Click Fumarate Polymers for Bone Tissue Engineering.
title: A click-chemistry fumarate scaffold that degrades as bone grows in
blurb: An organic-inorganic hybrid built from click-coupled fumarate polymers, pitched as a biodegradable scaffold that responds to new bone growth for tissue engineering.

original_title: Pyridine–Boryl Radical-Mediated [2σ + 2π] Cycloaddition Reactions of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with Pyridines and Quinolines
title: Boryl radicals stitch pyridines onto bicyclobutanes
blurb: A pyridine-boryl radical drives a [2σ+2π] cycloaddition between bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes and pyridines or quinolines, then oxidizes and rearomatizes to hand you pyrido- and quinolino-fused bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, no metal needed. Broad scope and solid regioselectivity, yields land moderate to good rather than uniformly high.

original_title: Comparing electro- and thermo-catalytic ammonia decomposition, a crucial component in the green ammonia value chain as an H 2 vector
title: Ammonia-to-hydrogen: electro and thermo catalysis both land on Ru, for different reasons
blurb: A head-to-head of electro- and thermocatalytic ammonia decomposition, the de-hydrogenation step the whole green-ammonia-as-H2-carrier idea depends on. Ru wins both races but not for the same reason: electrochemically it's just better at driving anodic water and ammonia electrolysis, while on the thermal side a H2-permeable membrane lets you cut the operating temperature without losing activity. Ru still has its own drawbacks as the default metal, which the comparison doesn't paper over.

original_title: Rh-Catalyzed Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Fused Polycycles with 1,3-Nonadjacent Tetrasubstituted Stereocenters via C–C Bond Activation
title: Rh cracks a C-C bond to build stereocenters three atoms apart
blurb: An intramolecular Rh-catalyzed (4+2) annulation activates a C-C bond in benzocyclobutenols and fuses them with alkenes, building dihydrobenzofuran-cyclohexane scaffolds with two tetrasubstituted stereocenters sitting non-adjacent at 1,3, and still getting high diastereo- and enantioselectivity out of it. Full atom economy, mild conditions, and a follow-up reductive C-O cleavage turns the same sequence into a formal intermolecular (4+2) in disguise.

original_title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp 3 )–H Bond System
title: Getting alkyne-bearing cyclopropanes to actually polymerize
blurb: Ring-opening polymerization of cyclopropanes usually demands strongly push-pull substituents, which left alkynylcyclopropanes out since the triple bond's electronegativity and coordinating pull get in the way. Pairing a Lewis acid with a Brønsted base and a C(sp3)-H bond gets around that, opening a C3 polymerization route to these less-activated monomers toward all-carbon polymers.

original_title: Electrochemically-driven Deracemization of Tetrahydroisoquinolines
title: An electrochemical detour around the Bischler-Napieralski bottleneck
blurb: Enantiopure tetrahydroisoquinolines have mostly been stuck with Bischler-Napieralski cyclization plus asymmetric reduction as the one dominant route. This does it electrochemically instead, deracemizing the racemate directly rather than building the stereocenter from scratch.

original_title: Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling of Indoles with Fluorinated Primary Alcohols through Cocatalysis of DMAP and Na2CO3
title: Bolting fluorinated alcohols onto indoles without a metal catalyst
blurb: DMAP and Na2CO3 cocatalyze a dehydrogenative coupling that installs fluorinated primary alcohols, from trifluoroethanol up to heptafluorobutanol, at indole's C3 position, with yields reported up to >99% on the best substrates. Holds up with the usual halogens and esters sitting on the ring, which matters more than that headline yield once you try it on something real.

original_title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
title: Lopsided gold nanoclusters get a second active site
blurb: An Au39 nanocluster built with pyridyl-phosphine and alkynyl ligands, where swapping in nitrogen donors breaks the usual symmetric alkynyl-Au-alkynyl motif and opens up a second, asymmetric coordination site next to it, confirmed by single-crystal X-ray. The two mismatched sites apparently cooperate on aerobic oxidation rather than one just riding along.

original_title: Radical S -Arylation of Sulfoxides Promoted by KO t Bu/DMSO
title: Diaryl sulfoxides, no metal required
blurb: KOtBu and DMSO under light generate aryl radicals straight from aryl iodides via an electron donor-acceptor complex, with DMSO itself acting as the electron donor, and those radicals attack sulfur to convert allyl aryl sulfoxides into diaryl sulfoxides. The mechanism is the interesting part; the transformation itself is a fairly plain swap.

original_title: Catalytic asymmetric construction of axially chiral silanes
title: Axially chiral silicon gets the chiral-axis treatment
blurb: A review covering catalytic asymmetric routes to axially chiral silanes, basically the silicon counterpart to the axially chiral biaryls everyone already works with. That's about all there is to go on here.

original_title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni 0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
title: A 3D-printed stirrer that doubles as the hydrogenation catalyst
blurb: Take a 3D-printed bladed agitator and hit its alloy surface with a molten-salt treatment that strips it down to exposed Ni0 sites while leaving the printed shape intact. The payoff is selective alkyne hydrogenation where the reactor's moving part and the catalyst are the same piece of metal, dodging the usual tradeoff between activity and structural durability under high-pressure liquid-phase conditions.

original_title: A Transferable Substrate-Pocket Stereochemical Switch Enables Stereocomplementary Alcohol Dehydrogenases for Asymmetric Reduction of N -Boc-Protected Cyclic Ketones
title: One residue flips which hand your alcohol comes out in
blurb: CgADH and its near-identical cousin CgKR1 reduce the same N-Boc ketone to opposite enantiomers, and comparing their structures pins the switch to a single substrate-pocket residue, F173. Swap it and you get a stereocomplementary pair of enzymes instead of having to screen for whichever one you need. Still shown on one substrate class so far, but a transferable single-residue switch is exactly what biocatalysis people want out of this kind of work.

original_title: Recent advances in the synthesis of boron-stereogenic compounds
title: A field guide to making boron centers that are actually chiral
blurb: Tetracoordinate boron is stereogenic and useful for optoelectronics and biomedicine, but reliable routes to build chiral versions have stayed scattered across the literature. This review sorts the catalytic methods by metal, copper, palladium, rhodium, nickel and cobalt among them, into one map. Handy if you're deciding which metal to reach for, though it's organizing existing chemistry rather than adding new reactions.

original_title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
title: Turning softwood lignin waste into a tumor-selective drug lead
blurb: A three-step sequence, catalytic depolymerization to a guaiacol, diazotization to an aminophenol, then photocatalytic cyclization, converts softwood lignin into a benzoxazole that's selectively toxic to tumor cells. 6.2 wt% overall yield of the final compound straight from raw lignin, which is a real number and makes lignin valorization look like more than the usual biofuel afterthought.

original_title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
title: One imidazolium monomer gets flame retardant, antistatic, and recyclable into the same polyester
blurb: Those properties usually come from separate additives bolted on afterward, which is also where the migration and leaching problems come from. Here a single imidazolium monomer builds flame retardancy and antistatic behavior straight into the backbone, solvent-free, while keeping color, heat resistance and strength intact, and the resin still sorts cleanly out of mixed waste for recycling. The additive-free part is the actual point, not just another green-chemistry checkbox.

original_title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables Sn II /Sn IV Redox Catalysis
title: A tin cation that's actually two-coordinate, and it actually does redox
blurb: Two-coordinate stannyliumylidenes should make good ambiphilic redox catalysts thanks to their exposed lone pair and empty p-orbital, but every prior example needed a rigid pi- or heteroatom-stabilized cage just to survive isolation. This one is acyclic and genuinely two-coordinate, and it cycles between Sn(II) and Sn(IV). Getting both the stability to isolate it and the flexibility to actually cycle oxidation states in the same molecule is the hard part they pulled off.

original_title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
title: Pairing Ru with Fe keeps methane oxidation from going feral
blurb: Fe/H2O2 methane oxidation usually loses selectivity because the methyl and hydroxyl radicals it generates react with whatever's nearby. Co-loading atomically dispersed Ru with Fe in ZSM-5 gives the hydroxyl radical somewhere to park instead, steering the chemistry toward coupling inside the micropores. That buys 37.5 mmol/g/h of oxygenates at a mild 70°C, with 92.3% of the liquid product landing as formic acid specifically. Selective methane-to-formic-acid without routing through syngas, and the numbers actually back it up.

original_title: Organic Heterogeneous Electrosynthesis: Interfacial Catalysis for Selective Organic Transformations
title: A framework for making sense of electrode-surface organic chemistry
blurb: Organic heterogeneous electrosynthesis has grown fast enough that sorting it by catalyst material or reaction type stopped being useful. This review proposes a site-interface-pathway framework instead, built around four interfacial modes that tie catalyst design to the selectivity you actually get out. A conceptual tidy-up rather than new chemistry, but a subfield growing this fast needed one.

original_title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO 2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
title: CO2 finally gets a perfectly alternating copolymer partner
blurb: Most CO2-derived polyesters rely on carbonate linkages arranged randomly or in blocks. Terpolymerizing CO2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides instead gives a strictly alternating CO2-cyclosilane-epoxide sequence, driven by how favorable Si-O bond formation is. The payoff is a poly(silyl ether-ester) with a defined backbone architecture that's still recyclable, not just another statistical CO2 copolymer.

original_title: Selective Reduction of Interchain Disulfides in Native Antibodies is an Underexplored Problem
title: Antibody disulfides: nobody's bothered to reduce just one pair
blurb: Native IgG1 has four interchain disulfides, two H-H in the hinge and two H-L, and conjugation chemistry has mostly only learned to use all of them for DAR4 or DAR8 ADCs. Selectively reducing just one pair would give finer control over drug loading and open up dual-payload ADCs without redesigning the linker or engineering the antibody, but apparently almost nobody's tried it.

original_title: Chain-Specific Drug Antibody Ratio and Conjugation Site Localization by Native Top-Down Mass Spectrometry
title: One MS run for DAR, which chain, and where the payload sits
blurb: A native top-down mass spec workflow that pulls intact DAR, chain-specific DAR, and partial modification site localization out of a single analysis, instead of stitching together separate intact, reduced-chain, subunit, and peptide-level runs. Fewer workflows to validate, if it holds up past this paper.

original_title: ADCdb 2.0: clinical landscape and ADMET profiles of antibody–drug conjugates
title: A bigger lookup table for ADCs
blurb: ADCdb 2.0 bolts clinical pipeline data and ADMET profiles onto the existing target and indication info, aiming to be one place to check an ADC's profile instead of hunting across trial registries. A reference update, not a result.

original_title: Merging substrate permissive biocatalysis with chemical derivatization to build post-translationally modified lipidated peptides
title: Enzymes handle the weird crosslinks, click chemistry handles the lipid
blurb: Promiscuous enzymes install lanthionine crosslinks and azole heterocycles on peptides, then diazotransfer and copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition bolt the lipid on afterward. Splits the job between biocatalysis's picky substrates and chemistry's wider tolerance to get lipidated, post-translationally modified peptides neither side could build on its own.

original_title: Implementing [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in clinical practice: a multistakeholder evaluation of real-world experience and implementation challenges.
title: Lu-177-PSMA-617 in the clinic, past the trial numbers
blurb: A multistakeholder look at what actually happens rolling out Lu-177-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in practice, not phase 3 topline results. The implementation headaches sound like as much of the story as the drug itself.

original_title: A review of synthetic strategies for macrocyclic bifunctional chelators in molecular imaging and radiopharmaceutical applications.
title: How people actually build macrocyclic chelators
blurb: A review rounding up synthetic routes to macrocyclic bifunctional chelators used in imaging and radiopharmaceuticals. Reference reading, not new chemistry.

original_title: Comparison of [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE and [18F]MFBG PET/CT in SDHD-associated paraganglioma: Identifying multifocal disease and localizing the secretory lesion
title: Two tracers, one paraganglioma, figuring out which lesion is secreting
blurb: Ga-68-DOTATATE and F-18-MFBG PET/CT compared head to head in SDHD-associated paraganglioma, specifically for catching multifocal disease and localizing the actual secretory lesion. The kind of tracer-choice question that matters more at the clinic than in a methods paper.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: FcRn Silencing Accelerates Clearance of an LRRC15-Targeted [177Lu]Lu-Radioimmunoconjugate, Reducing Therapeutic Efficacy without Alleviating Hematologic Toxicity in Mice
title: Clearing the antibody faster just made it weaker, not safer
blurb: Silencing FcRn sped clearance of an LRRC15-targeted Lu-177 radioimmunoconjugate in mice, which should cut off-target toxicity by shortening circulation. Instead it tanked efficacy and left the hematologic toxicity right where it was. A clean negative result against the idea that faster clearance buys you a better safety margin.

original_title: Optical Scintillation Imaging for Dynamic Source Tracking Dosimetry During Prostate HDR Brachytherapy
title: Watching the brachytherapy source move instead of trusting the plan
blurb: A scintillator strip read through an endoscopic lens on a transrectal probe, tracking HDR source position, speed, and cumulative dose as it happens rather than assuming the planned trajectory held. Real-time in-vivo dosimetry for a procedure that currently flies blind between checks.

original_title: NET‐Inhibiting Bio‐Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence
title: Erasing a neutrophil's grudge to stop periodontitis from coming back
blurb: NETs turn out to be what locks in the trained immunity that makes periodontitis keep recurring, reprogramming bone marrow to overreact on the next flare. The fix here is a bioengineered platform, tPA@AGNs-DNase I, that inhibits NETs and reportedly erases that memory and blocks the recurrence.

original_title: A Critical Review of Protein Conjugation Strategies for Environmental Applications: Challenges and Opportunities
title: Pinning proteins to solid surfaces so you can actually reuse them
blurb: A review of protein immobilization strategies for things like breaking down pollutants, sensing, resource recovery, and disinfection. Free proteins deactivate and you can't easily fish them back out of solution, so the pitch is bolting them to a substrate. Whether that actually helps depends entirely on loading, attachment site, and whether the active site still points the right way, which is a messier answer than the title promises.

original_title: Amino acid-quinoline-engineered PSMA ligands for prostate cancer radiotheranostics.
title: Tweaking PSMA ligands with amino acid-quinoline chemistry
blurb: New PSMA-targeting ligands built around an amino acid-quinoline scaffold, aimed at prostate cancer radiotheranostics, the pair-diagnosis-with-treatment approach that PSMA imaging is built on.

original_title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
title: A cheap shortcut around coverage effects in catalysis
blurb: Crowded catalyst surfaces mean adsorbed molecules shove each other around and change the reaction energetics, which DFT chokes on combinatorially and machine learning needs mountains of training data for. The fix here is a physics-based linear correlation that maps those coverage-dependent adsorption energies straight onto cheap gas-phase pairwise interactions. If it generalizes, that's a lot of expensive calculations nobody has to run anymore.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT extends the vascular mapping of polyarteritis nodosa beyond [¹⁸F]FDG
title: FAPI-PET sees more vasculitis than FDG does
blurb: In polyarteritis nodosa, Ga-68-FAPI-46 PET/CT picks up vascular involvement that FDG PET misses, extending the mapped extent of disease. FAPI targets fibroblast activation rather than glucose uptake, so this plausibly catches something genuinely different rather than just being a more sensitive version of the same signal.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
title: Electrochemistry teams up with organocatalysis for fluorinated quaternary centers
blurb: α-Fluorinated quaternary stereocenters are a pain to make selectively because of steric and electronic clashes. This pairs chiral isothiourea organocatalysis with anodic single-electron oxidation to enantioselectively alkylate bench-stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. Worth noting it works across two different nucleophile classes under the same catalyst system rather than just one.

original_title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π ‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
title: Allylpalladium goes radical under visible light, then builds rings
blurb: Zwitterionic π-allylpalladium species usually only react with electrophiles or dipolarophiles. Here visible light homolytically cleaves the allylic C-Pd bond to generate Pd(I) plus an allylic radical, and that radical pathway opens up (4+2) annulations with ordinary 1,3-dienes and aryl-substituted enynes, partners that were off limits before. A genuinely new mode of reactivity for a well-worn intermediate, not just another substrate-scope paper.

original_title: Catalytic Asymmetric Carbamoylation: Carbamoyl Sources, Activation Modes, and Stereocontrol
title: A review of how to build chiral amides catalytically, carbamoyl group included
blurb: Chiral amides and lactams are everywhere in drugs and natural products but usually get made from preformed chiral building blocks. This rounds up catalytic asymmetric carbamoylation methods, organized by the carbamoyl source (formamides, carbamoyl halides, isocyanates, isocyanides), how it's activated, and where the stereocontrol comes from. A map of the field, not a new result.

original_title: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
title: A Suzuki-type coupling that skips palladium for radical oxalatoborates
blurb: Suzuki-Miyaura coupling gets aryl halides and organoborons to form C-C bonds just fine, but palladium brings its usual cost and ligand headaches. This swaps in radical oxalatoborates to run the same aryl halide/alkenyl boronic ester coupling through a noncanonical route. A complementary path to the same connectivity, useful for whichever case palladium is actually the bottleneck.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Optimisation of reconstruction parameters for lutetium-177 SPECT imaging: comparative performance of cadmium-zinc-telluride and NaI(Tl) detectors.
title: CZT vs NaI(Tl): tuning the reconstruction for Lu-177 SPECT
blurb: A head-to-head on reconstruction parameters for Lu-177 SPECT imaging, comparing cadmium-zinc-telluride detectors against the old standby NaI(Tl). Dry instrumentation work, but it's the kind of tuning that decides whether the dosimetry numbers you pull downstream are trustworthy.

original_title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti ‐Markovnikov Coupling of α ‐Methylene‐ γ ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
title: Thiophenol and light build aucklappalide A, no photocatalyst needed
blurb: Anti-Markovnikov coupling of electron-poor alkenes is usually hard to pull off selectively. A simple formate/thiophenol combo under visible light does it without a photocatalyst, assembling homo- and cross-coupled disesquiterpenoid lactones from complex sesquiterpenoid starting material, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A.

original_title: Autonomous AI-Robotics Design of High-Entropy Catalysts for the Urea Oxidation Reaction
title: An AI runs the robots to hunt down urea-oxidation catalysts
blurb: A closed loop where an LLM mines the literature and proposes candidates, theory-informed ML screens them, and a robot actually runs the high-throughput experiments on high-entropy Prussian blue analogues for urea oxidation. The point isn't one standout catalyst, it's outsourcing the search through a combinatorial space too big to brute-force by hand.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
title: A chiral radical route to silylated esters that actually works
blurb: First enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of alpha,beta-unsaturated esters, done by pairing photocatalytic bromine-radical HAT, which turns hydrosilanes into silyl radicals, with a chiral nickel catalyst that holds the resulting carbon radical long enough to set stereochemistry. Getting chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity out of a radical process all at once is the part that's eluded people until now.

original_title: Innovate UK £1.54m award for automated radiopharmaceutical production project - Laboratory News
title: Innovate UK puts £1.54M into automating radiopharmaceutical production
blurb: A grant to automate radiopharmaceutical manufacturing, the unglamorous infrastructure work that matters more day to day than any single new tracer.

original_title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
title: Finally wrangling radical hydrosilylation into being enantioselective
blurb: Radicals are good at hydrosilylation and bad at picking one enantiomer, which is why this hasn't been done before for electron-deficient alkenes. A photocatalyst generates bromine radicals to make silyl radicals via HAT, and a chiral nickel catalyst babysits the carbon-centered radical intermediate on alpha,beta-unsaturated esters long enough to lock in selectivity.

original_title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
title: Confinement trick turns CO and nitrate into an oxime
blurb: Direct electrosynthesis of acetaldoxime from CO and nitrate co-reduction, normally doomed because C-C dimerization crawls while nitrate reduction races ahead and dumps everything into ammonia instead. Confining the reaction environment rebalances that kinetic mismatch enough to get the C-N coupling to happen, a cleaner route to a feedstock usually made the dirty way.

original_title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO 2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
title: Sorting out which atoms in a CO2 hydrogenation catalyst are actually doing the work
blurb: Modulation excitation spectroscopy separates the catalytically active species from the spectator ones during CO2 hydrogenation, where bulk spectroscopy normally averages real intermediates in with inert surface dressing. A methods paper rather than a new catalyst, but knowing which sites to target is half of designing a better one on purpose.

original_title: Biopolymer Hydrogels, Biochar, and Bio-based Plastics: A Review
title: A grand tour of hydrogels, biochar, and bioplastics
blurb: A review stitching together three bio-based materials that mostly have in common that they're not petroleum, with mechanical performance and scalability flagged as the recurring weak point across all three.

original_title: Photocatalytic Cross-Coupling of Sulfoxonium Ylides with Silyl Enol Ethers for the Synthesis of 1,4-Diketones
title: Building 1,4-diketones without a whiff of metal
blurb: Visible-light coupling of sulfoxonium ylides with silyl enol ethers makes 1,4-diketones using just the organic photocatalyst 4CzIPN, no metal, base, or additive involved. That matters specifically because 1,4-diketones feed into organic optoelectronics, where trace metal contamination is exactly the kind of thing that tanks device performance, and the scope reportedly covers aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic partners.

original_title: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
title: Does adsorbed CO actually do the C-N coupling in urea electrosynthesis?
blurb: *CO is the intermediate everyone assumes drives C-N bond formation in CO2/nitrate co-reduction to urea on copper, but nobody had watched it do the coupling directly. Combining surface-enhanced IR with ab initio MD to track *CO coverage mid-reaction, which is to say actually testing an assumption the field had mostly taken on faith.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective Heterobenzylation of gem -Difluorocyclopropanes via C–C Bond Cleavage of Tertiary Aza-benzyl Alcohols
title: Swapping fluoroalkenes onto azaarenes via a C-C bond you wouldn't expect to break
blurb: Palladium ring-opens gem-difluorocyclopropanes and couples them with aza-benzyl alcohols, which act here as benzyl-transfer reagents by having their unstrained C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond cleaved through N-chelation assistance. An odd bond to target, but it delivers regioselective installation of fluoroalkene fragments on azaarenes, backed up with a scale-up run and downstream derivatization.

original_title: Quantitative pulmonary [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a prospective proof-of-concept PET/CT study
title: A PET tracer that finds hypoxic lung tissue CT can't see
blurb: Ten IPF patients and ten age-matched healthy controls got FMISO PET/CT, a tracer that lights up hypoxic tissue rather than just structural scarring. Uptake tracked with CT abnormalities and lung function in this cross-sectional look, but it's a proof-of-concept with ten people a side, so call it a hypothesis generator, not a biomarker yet.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: PCET beyond p K a : Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
title: The base matters more than the pKa in this O-H activation
blurb: MS-PCET activation of cycloalkanol O-H bonds has mostly needed electron-rich PMP-type arenes to even work, which locks out a lot of substrates. Here the limiting factor wasn't the alcohol's acidity but how aggregated the base is in solution, and tuning the base partner opens up previously inaccessible, non-activated substrates for the ring-opening remote alkylation.

original_title: Chemotype-Symmetric Junction-Tree VAE for SARS-CoV-2 Mpro Inhibitor Design
title: Keeping nirmatrelvir's warhead while scoring it safer
blurb: A junction-tree VAE for designing Mpro inhibitors that explicitly protects the reactive warhead and the fused-aromatic scaffold, the two things standard drug-likeness scoring tends to optimize away or choke on generating validly. It improves predicted safety while keeping the warhead and target affinity intact, on paper. Generative design, so it's predictions until something actually gets synthesized.

original_title: Exploiting the Full Redox Capacity of g-C3N4 in Heterogeneous Photochemically Driven Synthesis of Trifluoroethyl-Substituted Alkenes from Morita–Baylis–Hillman Acetates
title: g-C3N4 pushed through both ends of its redox range for CF3 alkenes
blurb: Trifluoroethyl-substituted alkenes made by reacting Morita-Baylis-Hillman acetates with CF3 radicals from Langlois' reagent, run on heterogeneous carbon nitride under 450 nm light. The point is wringing the full oxidation and reduction capacity of g-C3N4 out of one ion-radical cascade instead of using it as a one-way oxidant.

original_title: Catalyst‐Free Annulation of Sulfoxonium Ylides With Quinone Imides: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Indolines and Dihydrobenzofurans
title: No catalyst needed to choose indolines or dihydrobenzofurans
blurb: Sulfoxonium ylides plus quinone diimides or monoimides, no catalyst, no additive, room temperature, and which quinone you pick switches the product: indolines from one, dihydrobenzofurans from the other, both coming out at better than 20:1 dr. It scales to grams too, which for a catalyst-free annulation is the actual selling point.

original_title: Construction of Chiral Piperidine Scaffold through an Enantioselective (8+3)-Cycloaddition of Donor-Acceptor Cyclopropanes with Azaheptafulvenes
title: Donor-acceptor cyclopropanes as three-carbon units for chiral piperidines
blurb: A Brønsted base catalyzed (8+3) cycloaddition pairs donor-acceptor cyclopropanes with azaheptafulvenes to build chiral piperidine scaffolds enantioselectively, with the cyclopropane acting as a three-carbon building block instead of the usual one or two.

original_title: ITM and AtomVie Global Radiopharma Enter Supply Agreement for n.c.a. Lutetium-177 - Yahoo Finance UK
title: ITM locks down more non-carrier-added Lu-177 supply
blurb: A supply agreement between ITM and AtomVie for n.c.a. lutetium-177, the isotope behind most of the current crop of targeted radioligand therapies. More a capacity-chain story than a science one, but whoever controls n.c.a. Lu-177 supply controls whose trials actually stay on schedule.

original_title: Atroposelective synthesis of biaryls with artificial SNAr enzymes
title: Enzymes evolved for point chirality get repointed at chiral axes
blurb: SNArases originally built to set point-chiral centers get repurposed to construct axially chiral biaryls instead, via two enantiocomplementary NTF2-like enzymes that differ by just four mutations. Axial chirality shows up constantly in bioactive compounds and chiral catalysts, and biocatalysts for it are rare, so getting both enantiomers from four mutations is the notable part.

original_title: Beyond Conventional Chemistry: Unlocking the Potential of Thioamides Through Photo‐, Electro‐, and Photoelectrochemical Approaches
title: Thioamides get the photo/electro treatment usually reserved for amides
blurb: A roundup of ways to activate thioamides, the sulfur-swapped amide isostere, without the usual harsh heat and stoichiometric oxidants, covering photo-, electro-, and photoelectrochemical routes that lean on the sulfur's nucleophilicity and redox behavior instead. It's a perspective piece, so judge it by whether it gets people reaching for thioamides more, not by any single new reaction.

original_title: Split crRNA-Programmed Cas12a-Cleavable DNA Hydrogel Paper Chip for Distance-Based Visual Quantification of miRNA
title: Reading miRNA levels off a paper chip, no instrument required
blurb: A split-crRNA Cas12a system drives a DNA hydrogel read out as a visual distance on a paper chip, for miRNA-21 and miRNA-622. The split-crRNA trick targets the usual CRISPR biosensor problem, leaky background signal, pushing the readout from qualitative yes/no toward actual quantification.

original_title: [2 + 2]‐Cycloaddition: An Approach to Cyclobutane‐/Azetidine‐Containing Bicyclic Amines and Lactams
title: Two decades of [2+2] tricks for making bicyclic amines, in one place
blurb: A rundown of how people build cyclobutane- and azetidine-fused bicyclic amines and lactams via [2+2] cycloaddition, split into intermolecular routes (imines or cyclic amines/maleimides meeting alkenes or alkynes under light, heat, or catalysis) and intramolecular ones (bisallylamines closing head-to-head or head-to-tail). More a map of the playbook than a new reaction.

original_title: Photoinduced Selective Oxidative γ-Hydroxylation of Pyrrolidone
title: Lighting up pyrrolidones at the gamma position, no metal needed
blurb: Visible light excites a dicarbonyl compound into a triplet biradical that pulls a hydrogen off pyrrolidone's gamma carbon, and the resulting iminium gets trapped by water to install a hydroxyl right where C-H functionalization usually stalls out. Mild and metal-free, going after a spot that's normally dead weight.

original_title: Generation of triarylmethyl cations and oxygen nucleophiles from triarylmethanol derivatives for hydride-abstraction-mediated transformations
title: Triarylmethanols as hydride traps, with acyl fluorides as the payoff
blurb: Triarylmethanol derivatives generate triarylmethyl cations that abstract hydride, opening up a batch of transformations. The one they actually show off is building acyl fluorides from o-hydrosilyl benzotrifluorides via C-F cleavage.

original_title: Alkyne‐Based Glycosyl Donors in Glycosidic Bond Formation
title: Nearly twenty years of putting an alkyne handle on glycosyl donors
blurb: A review tracing how bolting an alkynyl group onto the anomeric leaving group grew into a whole donor platform, from propargyl glycosides and hexynoates to ortho-alkynylbenzoates, mostly fired by pi-acid catalysis with Au, Ag, or Hg, with some Brønsted acid versions too. A survey of what exists, not a new result.

original_title: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes map onto distinct cholinergic and serotonergic territories in autoimmune encephalitis
title: FDG-PET tracks where autoimmune encephalitis actually eats into the brain
blurb: Longitudinal FDG-PET changes in autoimmune encephalitis map onto distinct cholinergic and serotonergic territories rather than looking like diffuse inflammation, which is a tidier story than the usual hand-wave.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Pore-Resolved High-Throughput Analysis of Amyloid Aggregation and Amplification
title: Counting amyloid fibrils one pore at a time
blurb: ThT assays give you one bulk number for fibril content, but the APQ chip partitions samples across thousands of pores and reads the ThT fluorescence distribution in each, so you get the clustering and amplification structure that a bulk readout averages away. Higher-throughput look at how amyloid builds up, not just how much there is.

original_title: Active-Methylene Oxidation of Boraanthracene Acceptors: A Single-Atom Edit to Donor-Switchable Solid-State Luminescence
title: One oxygen swapped into a boraanthracene changes how the whole thing glows
blurb: Oxidizing the methylene bridge in a boraanthracene acceptor turns it into a carbonyl-bridged emitter, dropping the LUMO by 0.8-0.9 eV, switching on aggregation-induced emission, and pushing solid-state emission out to 700 nm. The donor decides the mechanism: carbazole gives room-temperature phosphorescence, acridan gives thermally activated delayed fluorescence, both tracing back to the donor-acceptor dihedral angle. A single-atom edit carrying a surprising amount of the result.

original_title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
title: Triptycene COFs that actually show up as well-faceted crystals
blurb: Three new triptycene-based COFs built from rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic nodes, grown as micrometer-sized, well-faceted crystals in under 24 hours under mild conditions. 3D COFs past simple tetrahedral nodes usually come out as crystalline mush, so the faceted crystals are the actual news.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
title: An engineered enzyme that forces electrocyclization to go antarafacial
blurb: Enzymes doing electrocyclizations are rare to begin with. This artificial photoenzyme pins acrylanilide substrates through a network of hydrophobic contacts into a geometry that forces a selective, enantioselective antarafacial 6pi-electrocyclization, less a product showcase than a proof that you can engineer a protein to dictate which pathway a photoreaction takes.

original_title: Synergistic CHA and CRISPR/Cas12a Amplification−Enhanced SERS Biosensor for Sensitive ctDNA Detection in Lung Cancer
title: Cas12a's trans-cleavage wired up as a kill switch for a SERS signal
blurb: Catalytic hairpin assembly turns a ctDNA hit into a pile of duplexes that switch on Cas12a's trans-cleavage, which then shreds linker ssDNA and knocks the SERS nanoprobes off their programmed assembly. Another layered amplification scheme for spotting NSCLC mutations, just with SERS doing the reading instead of fluorescence.

original_title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
title: Letting degraders pick their own E3 ligase for once
blurb: A 114-compound BRD4-targeting bifunctional library screened straight off the synthesis plate, no purification detour, and the hits didn't all funnel through the usual handful of E3 ligases everyone defaults to. That's the whole point of a degrader-first screen: you surface noncanonical mechanisms you'd never have designed for.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]AlF-FAPI-JR11: A Novel Heterodimeric PET Tracer Targeting Fibroblast Activation Protein and Somatostatin Receptor 2
title: A PET tracer trying to cover both the tumor and its scaffolding
blurb: [18F]AlF-FAPI-JR11 links an SSTR2 antagonist to a FAP-binding arm so one scan hits tumor cells and the stromal fibroblasts around them, aimed at the patchy receptor expression that trips up single-target imaging in neuroendocrine tumors. One-step radiolabeling, over 95% purity, docking simulations say the dual binding is geometrically plausible. Still preclinical.

original_title: Automated Radiosynthesis, Preclinical Validation, and First-in-Human PET Evaluation of the SSTR2 Antagonist [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-PEG2-JR11
title: A second-gen SSTR2 tracer that's already made it into a person
blurb: [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-PEG2-JR11 swaps in a tweaked linker and beats its predecessor on cellular and xenograft uptake, with automated radiosynthesis down to about 40 minutes and over 98% purity. Unlike most of these tracer papers, this one got to first-in-human PET, not just mice.

original_title: Preclinical comparison of B7-H3-targeted 177Lu-radioimmunoconjugates based on self-developed and ifinatamab-based antibodies
title: Does the branded B7-H3 antibody actually beat the homemade one
blurb: A head-to-head of 177Lu-labeled B7-H3 radioimmunoconjugates built on a self-developed antibody versus one based on ifinatamab, the binder behind the B7-H3 ADC everyone's watching. Preclinical comparison, so no verdict yet on whether the branded antibody is worth chasing over rolling your own.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Single-sample-calibrated image-derived pharmacokinetics of the PD-L1-targeted tracer [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 using total-body PET: Beyond conventional venous blood sampling
title: Skipping the serial blood draws for PET pharmacokinetics
blurb: A way to pull image-derived pharmacokinetics for the PD-L1 tracer [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 straight off total-body PET, calibrated from a single blood sample instead of the usual run of venous draws. Less blood for roughly the same curve.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Trans-Picolinate Functionalization of a Cyclen-Based Chelator Enables Complexation of Large Radiometals for Cancer Theranostics.
title: A cyclen chelator modified to finally hold the big radiometals
blurb: Trans-picolinate arms grafted onto a cyclen cage so it can complex the larger radiometals that DOTA-style chelators usually struggle to cage properly, with cancer theranostics as the intended use. Chemistry-first paper, no biology yet.

original_title: Open Microfluidic Probe Enabled Regional Surface Modification of Single Cells by Click Chemistry.
title: Editing one cell's surface at a time with an open microfluidic probe
blurb: An open microfluidic probe runs click chemistry on just one region of a single cell's surface instead of bathing the whole dish, the kind of spatial control bulk functionalization can't touch.

original_title: Visualizing periarticular inflammation of the shoulder and pelvic girdles in polymyalgia rheumatica with [(68)Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT.
title: Mapping where polymyalgia rheumatica actually inflames
blurb: [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT images periarticular inflammation around the shoulders and pelvic girdles in polymyalgia rheumatica, giving an actual picture of where the disease sits instead of inferring it from symptoms.

original_title: Azide-Alkyne Click Crosslinking Enables Increased Protein Loading in Enzyme-Encapsulated Core-Shell Nanofibers.
title: More enzyme per nanofiber, courtesy of click chemistry
blurb: Azide-alkyne crosslinking bumps up how much enzyme gets packed into core-shell nanofibers without it leaking back out, which is usually the bottleneck in these encapsulated-enzyme setups.

original_title: Efficacy and bystander effects of EGFR-targeting 40H3 antibody-drug conjugates in glioblastoma PDX models.
title: An EGFR antibody-drug conjugate that kills glioblastoma cells it's not even bound to
blurb: The 40H3 ADC targets EGFR in glioblastoma PDX models and shows a bystander effect, killing neighboring cells that don't express the target. That matters a lot in GBM, where EGFR expression is notoriously patchy tumor to tumor.

original_title: Refining risk assessment in 177 Lu-DOTATATE extravasation: the value of 3D Monte Carlo dosimetry.
title: Modeling what happens when Lu-177 misses the vein
blurb: 3D Monte Carlo dosimetry for estimating the actual tissue dose from a Lu-177-DOTATATE extravasation, a step up from the cruder dose estimates typically used to decide how worried to be about an infiltrated injection.

original_title: End-to-End Continuous Flow Synthesis of a Bench-Stable Sulfamoylating Reagent: Application to the Preparation of a Key Edoxaban Intermediate
title: Flow chemistry tames the Burgess reagent's cranky cousin
blurb: The N-Boc sulfamoylating reagent is great for installing sulfamate and sulfamide groups but never scaled up because it won't sit on a shelf and its precursor is a labile, violently exothermic chloride. An end-to-end continuous flow process fixes both problems at once, spitting out a crystalline, bench-stable version, used here to build a key Edoxaban intermediate. Process chemistry, not a new reaction, but the kind that actually matters for manufacturing.

original_title: Next-Generation Bioconjugate Design Calls for an Orthogonal Analytical Approach - Chromatography Online
title: Bioconjugates are getting fancier, so should the QC
blurb: The case for orthogonal analytical methods, several techniques cross-checking each other instead of one assay, as next-generation bioconjugate designs outgrow standard antibody-drug conjugate QC.

original_title: A Study of Raludotatug Deruxtecan (R-DXd) in People With Gastrointestinal Cancers (MK-5909-005)
title: Merck's R-DXd moves into GI cancers
blurb: A Phase 2 trial of raludotatug deruxtecan, Merck's antibody-drug conjugate, running in gastrointestinal cancers and already closed to new enrollment. A status update, not a data readout.

original_title: The Nitrile Imine Platform in Bioorthogonal Chemistry: No Perfect, But Better
title: Nitrile imines still aren't a perfect bioorthogonal handle
blurb: A review tracking nitrile imine [3+2] click chemistry from its flask-chemistry origins to today's bioorthogonal probes, cataloguing the full set of precursors, tetrazoles, hydrazonoyl halides, and the rest, pitched at organic and medicinal chemists who've mostly watched this field from the sidelines. The honest framing: better than the alternatives, not flawless.

original_title: Selective Reduction of Interchain Disulfides in Native Antibodies is an Underexplored Problem.
title: Nobody's figured out how to selectively reduce just some antibody disulfides
blurb: A paper arguing that selectively reducing interchain disulfides in native, unengineered antibodies, exactly the control you'd want for site-specific conjugation, remains a poorly solved problem despite how often people need it.

original_title: Internalizing-peptide engineering converts blocking anti-EGFR antibodies into EGFR lysosomal targeting degraders
title: Turning cetuximab from a blocker into a degrader
blurb: Conjugating cetuximab to the polyarginine peptide R12 drags the antibody-EGFR complex into the cell instead of just parking on the surface blocking it, cutting both surface and total EGFR levels. A way to convert an existing antagonist antibody into an actual receptor-depleting one without starting from scratch.

original_title: Comparison of [(68)Ga]Ga-DOTATATE and [(18)F]MFBG PET/CT in SDHD-associated paraganglioma: Identifying multifocal disease and localizing the secretory lesion.
title: Two tracers, one hunt for hidden paraganglioma
blurb: A head-to-head of Ga-68-DOTATATE and F-18-MFBG PET/CT in SDHD-associated paraganglioma, aimed at catching multifocal disease and pinning down which lesion is actually secreting hormones. A tracer shootout that matters more for this rare SDHD subtype than for sporadic cases.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Characterization of GPR56/ADGRG1 as a target for antibody-drug conjugate therapy in triple-negative breast cancer.
title: A new ADC target for triple-negative breast cancer
blurb: Characterizing GPR56/ADGRG1 as an antigen antibody-drug conjugates could target in triple-negative breast cancer. Target validation, not a therapeutic candidate yet.

original_title: Quantum-Mechanics-guided covalent recruitment of FBXO22 enable dual-protein degradation
title: Found a new E3 ligase warhead by actually calculating it
blurb: Targeted protein degradation is bottlenecked by the small handful of E3 ligases anyone actually uses, CRBN and VHL, and losing either one is a known resistance route. This uses a quantum-mechanics-guided search to find 4-fluoro-3-nitrobenzamide as a covalent warhead for FBXO22, an unexploited ligase, then wires it onto JQ1 to make a molecular glue degrader that knocks down two proteins at once. A genuinely new ligase handle, not just another CRBN degrader with a different logo.

original_title: Merck-Kelun ADC scores survival win in Phase 3 gastroesophageal cancer trial - BioSpace
title: Merck-Kelun's ADC posts a survival win in gastric cancer
blurb: Their antibody-drug conjugate hit overall survival in a Phase 3 trial for gastroesophageal cancer. That's the headline for now; the actual hazard ratios haven't surfaced yet.

original_title: Clinical Modality of Resistance to Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (T-DXd) and Outcomes of Post-T-DXd Treatment in Patients With Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
title: What happens after trastuzumab deruxtecan stops working
blurb: A retrospective look at how metastatic breast cancer patients progress once they develop resistance to T-DXd, and how they fared on whatever came next. Chart review, not a trial, so the patterns are hypothesis-generating rather than settled.

original_title: Biomimetic cell membrane coated lipid nanoparticles: Advances in design and application in drug delivery
title: Dressing lipid nanoparticles in real cell membranes
blurb: A review of coating liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, and NLCs with actual cell membrane components to dodge the immune clearance and poor targeting that plain lipid formulations run into. It's a round-up of design advances rather than new data, but a decent map of where the field keeps patching LNPs' usual weak points.

original_title: Iron-Photocatalysed Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Coupled with Nickel-Catalysed SH2 for Decarboxylative sp3–sp3 Coupling of Free Carboxylic Acids and NHPI Esters
title: Decarboxylative coupling without palladium, an oxidant, or a base
blurb: Near-UV light excites an iron-carboxylate complex to kick off the decarboxylation, and a nickel catalyst closes the loop by bimolecular homolytic substitution, so two alkyl fragments from a carboxylic acid and an NHPI ester couple without precious metals, stoichiometric base, or an external oxidant. Just a splash of trifluoroethanol to help it along. Cheap catalysts doing a job that usually demands expensive ones.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Radical Relay Cyclization/Carbonylation of Bromoamide-Tethered Alkenes
title: CO gas turns bromoamide alkenes into lactams two different ways
blurb: A palladium-catalyzed radical relay cyclization/carbonylation running at just 1 atm of CO, branching into aminocarbonylation with amines or carbonylative arylation with arylboronic acids to build carbonyl-functionalized lactams. Broad substrate scope by their account, and the radical relay steps are mapped out mechanistically rather than just assumed.

original_title: A Dual-Crosslinked Coating with a Stable Self-generating Hydrogel Surface and Suppressed Water Permeation for Intrinsic Marine Antifouling.
title: A coating that keeps regrowing its own antifouling skin
blurb: A dual-crosslinked coating that continuously regenerates a fresh hydrogel surface while blocking water from soaking through, pitched as intrinsic marine antifouling. No performance numbers at hand, just the pitch.

original_title: An Automated Platform for Carbamate Functionalization of DNA and RNA Oligonucleotides
title: Automating the carbamate link for DNA and RNA conjugates
blurb: A fully automated solid-phase platform for building carbamate linkages on oligonucleotides, using a programmable DSC and N-methylimidazole cycle instead of the manual workflows carbamate chemistry usually demands. Handy if you're cranking out a lot of oligonucleotide conjugates and don't want to babysit each one.

original_title: Association of coronary 68Ga-DOTATATE uptake with CCTA-derived plaque burden in patients without prior cardiovascular events
title: A neuroendocrine tumor tracer snoops on heart plaque inflammation
blurb: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET binds SSTR2 on inflammatory macrophages, and in 40 people with no prior cardiovascular events its coronary uptake tracked with plaque features seen on CT angiography. Small, asymptomatic cohort, so it reads as proof-of-concept for catching inflamed plaque before an event, not a screening tool yet.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging
